reviews.text: Aphrodite best part of the game

This game is a diamond in the rough, but frustrating game mechanics stop it from being one of the best game's I've played in recent times. I'm a lover of roguelikes, soulslikes, and all that jazz. I found this game when one of my favourite YouTubers Beelz featured it in a video. Got this game IMMEDIATELY because it looked so fun, and I was right. This game's super fun. The labyrinth is amazing, and is so much bigger than I thought. The game is a cat-and-mouse style game where you're a bumbling idiot thrown into the labyrinth and the legendary Minotaur is hunting you down. You have to run around, gear up and get ready to fight him before he finds you. It's an amazing concept, and being spotted by the Minotaur, despite the game's goofy and charming art style, elicits a truly primal fear in me that I've only gotten from the greatest survival-horror games. But having played and mastered almost every rogue-souls-metroidvania-like-whatever game on the market, this game has some REAL pain points that, despite the game's marketed replayability, has discouraged me from trying to slay the Minotaur a second time. The BIGGEST criticism of this game is the Minotaur himself. One he finds you, the run is over, and unless you're fully kitted out, it's GG. He was scary the first couple times he found (and subsequently butchered) me. After about the fifth time, I realised that you can't ever out-run, escape, hide from or (most importantly) DE-AGGRO the Minotaur. The run IS OVER once he spots you, and that can be 10 minutes in, or more-or-less around the first corner when you spawn. I thought I did an amazing play by jumping over a gap to get to a completely different area of the labyrinth, hoping I would finally lose him, but no, the Minotaur just pathfinded around the entire labyrinth at mach-10 to exactly where I was. The Minotaur is extremely unfair. I only beat him by cheesing him, speedrunning my way to +3 movement speed and pelting him to death with projectiles from the Athlete's Spear. It didn't feel fun, and it took away from all of the Minotaur's very commanding stage-presence from the beginning of the game. Eventually he felt more like an annoyance than a frightening monster. Some other minor issues: - The fact you can only use each shop once is very irritating, especially if you're a few pearls shy. If it were me designing the game, I'd have no restock button and make the shop go away once you've bought all the permanent upgrades. - When the Cyclopses, Gorgons and the Minotaur 'launch' you with heavy attacks, it can soft-lock you if you get launched on top of an object such as a chest. - Gear is VERY imbalanced. Your dodge roll is a 'special ability' tied to your armour. Meaning you lose the ability to dodge by picking up most other helmets. Because of this, the Bronze, Silver and Gold defence helms are the only things worth getting. - Investing in stats can get out of control. If you pile on just one or two speed buffs and trigger some kind of conditional speed buff (such as from the helmet that gives a speed buff on successful parry), you quickly lose all control of your character. My guess is that this is an issue with multiplicative stat scaling. - No lock-on system in combat hurts, especially when trying to dodge circles around Cyclopses and Big M himself. Don't let all my criticisms of this game discourage you from getting it, however. For the price of just a chocolate bar or two, this game is a ton of fun and is absolutely hilarious. I streamed this game to my friends over discord and it made our evening. If this game improved on the Minotaur's AI, implemented some more random elements like different 'seeds' for the labyrinth, and added some QoL features like a universal dodge-roll and lock-on, this game has some serious potential and I'll humbly eat my words. I'm also gonna cut some slack because this is a single developer, and I respect them for doing something I have never had the motivation to start doing. And I'm SURE most of the things I've pointed out are on their ever-growing list of issues to fix. I'll keep a close eye on this game. and I can't wait to play it again.

Ok, so this game got a ton of influx after Youtubers like Wicked Wizard and such reviewed this game, and I was one of those people who saw such videos and thought "Wow, a pseudo souls-roguelike? Looks cool, is cheap enough, let me try it out." for the most part I can say the game is fine, but there are many, MANY critical problems with the game. Firstly, the balance is just a joke. Since none of the actually good items are randomised on the map, which itself also isn't random, it results in just beating up a cyclops for 45 or so damage at a time while avoiding their swings and taking their currency, running to one of the set good weapons or helmets, and then that's ALL YOU NEED TO DO FOR EQUIPMENT. Oh, but fear not, because even with the good equipment, you are almost guaranteed to die to some of the dumbest and most frustrating ♥♥♥♥ imaginable. I don't mean the death pits, that I can handle, but when you're casually fighting a ton of dudes, ONE of them being a living statue, and you die because it can't be flinched and it backs you into a corner and gangrapes you with 20 other dudes and you die DESPITE you having a helmet that's made for survival and a fast weapon with decent damage upgrades, yeah it's pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. It isn't even a fair annoying, where I want to learn and improve after the fact, because guess what? THERE'S NO SKILL TO THIS GAME, ONLY MAP KNOWLEDGE. Sure, learn how to parry, bet all the practice is sure to help you when the Minotaur finds you 2 minutes in while you have no upgrades and no hope of even running away. Oh yeah, another problem, most of the items in Aphrodite's shop are total dogwater. There are like what, 6 of the 20 or so upgrades she sells worth buying? Even the revive is terrible due to the fact that if you die while the Minotaur is chasing you and get revived at the start of the map, it will home in on your location like a pitbull named Buttercup and rip you a new one. Basically, if you don't have level 2 speed, and the Minotaur finds you, just Alt-F4 right then and there. Also, if you jump off the Coliseum tower and land on the large black rocks at the bottom because, y'know, you want to skip walking back down because you have the fall damage removal upgrade? Nope, ♥♥♥♥ you, you get to be deflected off the rocks like melted butter trying to climb the side of a skillet and die to the aforementioned death pit below. So yeah, the game has alot of problems, but a solid foundation. There are quite a few AI bugs, like how I got the cyclops to just keep doing the chest beating animation regardless of whether I was on the ground or not, or how the Minotaur can still get stuck on the edges of fire pits. Personally, I think that the best ways to improve the game would be to 1: Not have the Minotaur spawn in next to instantly. It can result in runs where you just catch his attention a few minutes in and are guaranteed to die, and that just isn't fun nor fair. I understand what purpose the Minotaur serves, it's like Mr. X from Resident Evil 2, a constantly pursuing enemy that's very imposing. But the difference with Mr. X and the Minotaur is the fact that Mr. X can be outran and the Minotaur cannot. Perhaps have the Minotaur upgrade alongside the player, have it be an enemy that's immortal WITHIN the general maze, but at certain areas have set boss encounters which give you breathing time afterwards but makes the Minotaur progressively stronger. That way, he is still a threat, still demands attention, but isn't instant death upon seeing him AND the game has way better pacing. 2: Randomise the gold chests. The map not being random is fine, IF the best items aren't 100% going to be exactly the same location wise every single damn time. Sadly that isn't the case, and the game devolves to the aforementioned cyclops bullying and Poseidon's Trident spam to kill the Minotaur after you get a few speed upgrades. I genuinely don't understand why this was done, because it doesn't "reward" players who memorise item locations in the same way Elden Ring doesn't "reward" players who spend the first 8 hours running around the map to get all their flask upgrades, it just trivialises the experience. 3: Finally, a general tweak to all the enemies in the game would be nice. Make arrows not lock you in place and physically push you out of cover or hiding spots from the Minotaur, have living statues be stunned after a few hits instead of not at all similar to how poise works in Fromsoft games, fix how cyclops' only resort to that one slam attack once they reach low health, and make gorgons actually somewhat fun instead of a wart on the experience. Finally finally, I get that this game is a "Diamond in the rough" or whatever, sure there's way worse ways to spend $8 or more, I'd take this over any dull-as-dirt EA ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ no matter what, but continually saying that this indie game is the second coming of Christ because it's a better game than the average NSFW game that always finds it's way to the store page is unproductive. This should be the baseline for what a game worth this much should be, and it should be treated as such. This isn't some amazing, incredible game, it's what the beta of games should strive to be. A finished product? Hell no, but it doesn't look like the dev has abandoned this game just yet, so maybe, just maybe, this game will become the definitive souls-rougelike on the market. Either that or it will end up as just plain meh, only time will tell.

The core mechanic this game is built around is stumbling blind into a Minotaur at complete random and dying with zero counterplay against a guy that is far faster than you and will never lose you no matter how hard you try. All you can do is hope that you randomly happen to not encounter him for long enough to get enough upgrades to stand a chance at killing him. There is an upgrade that tells you where he is... sometimes. When it feels like it. Which, more often than not, will be on those times when he's across the entire map rather than the times when he's just around the other corner about to rip you a structurally superfluous new behind. This is the core mechanic the entire game is built upon, and it is a 100% negative addition to the game, completely wrecking any chance of the game having any room to be fun. I could complain about other, smaller things, like the enemies popping up almost right on top of you half the time, or the parries feeling utterly unsatisfying to do, or the garbage jumping mechanics, or how incredibly dull the minotaur fight is when you do get lucky enough to win, but all the things I could list feel like petty complaints compared to the entire game being built upon one irredeemably garbage mechanic that sucks out all enthusiasm to continue. You will live and die purely on random chance. You live because the game allows it, and you will die because the game demands it. And either way, it will be painfully dull: either boring defeat or even more boring victory. And that is the greatest crime: wasting your bloody time. Stay the ♥♥♥♥ away from this game, if you value your time even as much you value the life of a fly in your kitchen. And ♥♥♥♥ you, Wicked Wizard.

However, as of now the combat feels too still and unprecise to me, the fact that you cannot flee from the minotaur once he's seen you once even by dropping down to another level is unfun and the constant spawning of enemies is also quite jarring at times. I really want to recommend this game but I just can't. It's too hard and punishing for absolutely no reason. After 2+ hours playing the game most runs still end up me dying <2 minutes in because the minotaur spawns too close and it's near impossible to run away. You pick up a helmet that half the time removes your dodge and makes you worse, and removing the dodge is just an instant death if you come across the minotaur. There's the makings of something really fun here but it's seems like there's just no way out if you see the minotaur early on, which seems to be pretty likely.

Sadly I cannot recommend this game to anyone yet. It's not quite polished enough to encourage a good time, it's just too challenging right now. A good run can be ruined in seconds, even at higher levels due to what feels like ridiculous enemy scaling, and the Minotaur can spawn in directly around a corner with no audio cues. Good idea for a game: needs more work before it gets fun.

A time sink, meat grinder, darksouls like all in one. The loop doesn't feel rewarding enough. The combat feels too clunky and inaccurate. The moment you see the Minotaur health bar just throw yourself into a pit and restart. Each run is completely RNG based, meaning you can easily run into enemies equipped with legendaries 2 minutes in or accidentally get the Minotaur to spawn directly in front of you 1 minute in. I think the dodge roll should at least enable a few more frames of invincibility and also pass through enemies or adjust their AI so they don't crowd you. This game needs a few quality of life updates and better upgrades. Maybe an option for more permanent upgrades? Tons of potential and I like the general premise, but needs work. I'll follow this games development, Although it likely will never get an update.

⚱️ Where's the fun? At first, it'll seem that the balance is insanely broken, but it's more likely just illusory. Always the same environment, with the same traps. You just need to memorize the path to the locations or take risks, which is often unjustified and only causes frustration. Some enemies are too easy, while others are simply impossible. LVLing is temporary, but it takes a lot of time, and the progress is barely noticeable. Item skills are either useless or completely broken, which is the main feature (you need to speedrun on pure luck). There is only 1-15 min max. before the Minotaur notices you. If he finds you, it's death, don't even try to escape, it's impossible (this is generally a problem with many tough enemies in the early stages). As a result, an uninteresting "Groundhog Day", with sometimes strange hit detection. It could have been worse, but the point is that it could've been better.
It's like playing one run in a rougelike, on the same map, with almost no differences.

This is a fun rogue-like third person action game. There is a surprising amount of depth in this game - from the combat, items, upgrades, enemy types, and even the map layout all keep the experience fresh. There is a bit of a learning curve, but there is an area where you can practice and try everything out to get acclimated to everything. I only just slayed the minotaur for the first time, and I can see that I am just scratching the surface for what is here. Highly recommend - lots of fun and a great value!

I've had a lot of fun with the game but there are some nitpicks that are incredibly grating. Foremost is that the enemy tracking is Dark Souls 2 level broken. Every enemy will pull complete 180 turns during a windup to land a hit on you after a dodge roll, it's ridiculous. The Cyclops' kick & the Minotaur's headbutt moves have no tell or windup at all. The Gorgon enemies are so tedious & have such tiny parry windows that the achievement for killing one is relatively low compared to everything else. It's glaring that bumping into the Minotaur without any upgrades means you'll be resetting the run. I've ran into the guy on the first turn before & the run didn't even last 15 seconds. This would be easily remedied by spawning him a certain distance away from the player, giving a small grace period. Not everyone is going to do a hardcore speedrun of the game & it's obnoxious to assume that. I really like how Aphrodite warms up to the player as she grows more confident in their skill, it's a small detail that goes a long way.
